The '''Celtics–Heat rivalry''' is a [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) [[National Basketball Association rivalries|rivalry]] between the [[Boston Celtics]] and the [[Miami Heat]]. It is widely regarded as one of the most intense postseason rivalries in NBA history.

Media writers generally state that the rivalry between the two teams solidified in the 2010s, after both teams formed "Big Threes" that began to face each other in multiple consecutive playoff matchups.

The two teams have met each other in four [[NBA Conference Finals#Eastern Conference Finals|Eastern Conference Finals]]: 2012, 2020, 2022, and 2023. All seven years the two teams have met in the postseason, the winner made the NBA Finals that year.

==History==

===1980s–2000s: Pre-rivalry years===
While the [[Boston Celtics]] [[History of the Boston Celtics|formed in 1946]], the [[Miami Heat]] began play in [[1988–89 NBA season|1988]] as an expansion franchise. The Celtics and Heat first played against each other on November 15, 1988; playing on the road, the Celtics defeated the Heat 84–65. Boston would win their first ten matchups against Miami.<ref name=LOB/>

An [[1990–91 NBA season|April 1991]] game between the two sides featured the Celtics' [[Reggie Lewis]] scoring a career high 42 points in a 119–109 victory for Boston.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tampabay.com/archive/1991/04/13/celtics-too-tough-for-miami-119-109/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230324034139/https://www.tampabay.com/archive/1991/04/13/celtics-too-tough-for-miami-119-109/|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 24, 2023|title=Celtics too tough for Miami 119–109|work=[[Tampa Bay Times]]|date=October 13, 2005|orig-date=April 13, 1991|accessdate=March 23, 2023}}</ref> In [[1995–96 NBA season|December 1995]], the Celtics narrowly won a double overtime game against the Heat 121–120.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.upi.com/Archives/1995/12/04/Celtics-121-Heat-120-2-OT/1687818053200/|title=Celtics 121, Heat 120 – 2 OT|publisher=[[United Press International]]|date=December 4, 1995|accessdate=March 23, 2023}}</ref>

In 1995, head coach [[Pat Riley]] resigned from the Knicks via fax to become president and head coach of the Miami Heat, with complete control over basketball operations. Riley's addition marked the moment the Miami Heat became an NBA Finals contender. Prior to a five-year run as Knicks coach, Riley was the head coach for the [[Showtime Lakers]] from 1981 to 1990 and a big part of the [[Celtics-Lakers rivalry]]. Riley, along with star players [[Dwyane Wade]] and [[Shaquille O'Neal]], would later lead the Heat to their first championship in franchise history in [[2006 NBA Finals|2006]].

From {{nbay|1989|start}} to {{nbay|2003|end}}, both teams played in the [[Atlantic Division (NBA)|Atlantic Division]], but after the Heat moved to the newly-formed [[Southeast Division (NBA)|Southeast Division]] as part of a [[2004–05 NBA season|2004 realignment]], they became intra-conference opponents.

===Boston and Miami's Big Threes===
The two teams met in the playoffs for the first time in [[2010 NBA playoffs|2010]], in the [[2010 NBA playoffs#(4) Boston Celtics vs. (5) Miami Heat|first round]]. The #4-seed Celtics were led by their [[Boston Celtics#2007–2012: New "Big Three": Pierce, Allen, and Garnett era|Big Three]] of [[Paul Pierce]], [[Ray Allen]], and [[Kevin Garnett]]. The #5-seed Heat were led by [[Dwyane Wade]], who averaged 33.2 points, 5.6 rebounds, and 6.8 assists in the series.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/playoffs/2010-nba-eastern-conference-first-round-heat-vs-celtics.html|title=2010 NBA Eastern Conference First Round Heat vs. Celtics |website=[[Sports Reference|basketball-reference.com]]|publisher=[[Sports Reference]]|accessdate=March 23, 2023}}</ref><ref name=Dill>{{cite web|last=Dill|first=Jason|url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/nba/miami-heat/article261490497.html|title=For the fifth time, Heat play Celtics in playoffs. Here's a look at their history.|work=[[The Miami Herald]]|date=May 16, 2022|accessdate=March 25, 2023}}</ref> During the first game of the series, Garnett elbowed Heat forward [[Quentin Richardson]], after Richardson walked up to Paul Pierce while injured insinuating Pierce was faking his injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/playoffs/2010/news/story?id=5109505|title=NBA reviewing Heat–Celtics skirmish|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=April 18, 2010|accessdate=March 23, 2023}}</ref><ref name=Moore>{{cite web|last=Moore|first=Matt|url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2010/04/18/kevin-garnett-suspended-for-game-2-versus-heat-for-elbow-altercation/|title=NBA Playoffs: Kevin Garnett suspended for Game 2 versus Heat for elbow altercation|publisher=[[NBC Sports]]|date=April 18, 2010|accessdate=March 23, 2023}}</ref> This led to an on-court dust-up between the two sides and as a result, Garnett received a suspension for game two of the series and Richardson was fined.<ref name=Moore/> In Game 4, Wade dropped 46 points to avoid getting swept. However, the Celtics won in five games.<ref name=Dill/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.patriotledger.com/story/sports/columns/2010/04/28/celtics-turn-focus-on-lebron/40163484007/|title=Celtics turn focus on LeBron and Cavaliers after eliminating Heat in five games|work=[[The Patriot Ledger]]|date=April 28, 2010|accessdate=March 24, 2023}}</ref>

During the subsequent offseason, the Heat signed [[LeBron James]] and [[Chris Bosh]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=5368003|title=Heat stars sign six-year deals|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=July 9, 2010|accessdate=March 24, 2023}}</ref> Along with Wade, the three formed [[Big Three (Miami Heat)|Miami's own "Big Three"]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Gleeson|first=Scott|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2012/10/23/lebron-james-dwyane-wade-chris-bosh-miami-heat-san-antonio-boston-celtics-spurs-big-three/1653275/|title=LeBron James, Dwyane Wade, Chris Bosh hardly first 'Big Three'|work=[[USA Today]]|date=October 23, 2012|accessdate=March 24, 2023}}</ref> James announced his decision to sign with the Heat in ''[[The Decision (TV program)|The Decision]]'', a television special that garnered him much criticism.<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Gregory|first=Sean|url=https://content.time.com/time/specials/packages/article/0,28804,2036683_2036767_2036799,00.html|title=People Who Mattered – LeBron James|magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]]|date=2010|accessdate=March 24, 2023}}</ref> In particular, James had developed a personal rivalry with the Celtics during his time with [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] as the Celtics eliminated the Cavaliers in the playoffs in 2008 and 2010.<ref name=Gregory>{{cite magazine|last=Gregory|first=Sean|url=https://keepingscore.blogs.time.com/2012/06/10/no-choke-lebron-james-and-miami-heat-move-one-step-closer-to-championship/|title=No Choke: LeBron James and Miami Heat Move One Step Closer to Championship|magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]]|date=June 10, 2012|accessdate=March 23, 2023}}</ref> NBA.com writer John Schuhmann wrote: "If the Celtics' big three didn't come together in 2007 via a pair of big trades, the Heat's big three probably wouldn't have come together last summer via free agency. Boston is the blueprint. Miami is the newer, more talented version."<ref>{{cite web|last=Schuhmann|first=John|url=http://www.nba.com/2011/news/features/john_schuhmann/04/28/celtics-heat-preview/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110502012944/http://www.nba.com/2011/news/features/john_schuhmann/04/28/celtics-heat-preview/index.html|title=The Main Event: East champ Boston vs. East challenger Miami|website=[[National Basketball Association|NBA.com]]|publisher=[[National Basketball Association]]|date=April 28, 2011|accessdate=March 23, 2023|archive-date=May 2, 2011}}</ref> The NBA scheduled the Celtics and Heat to play against each other for the [[2010–11 NBA season]]'s opening day.<ref name=Reindollar>{{cite web|last=Reindollar|first=Jason|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1258569-the-boston-celtics-and-miami-heat-are-officially-rivals|title=The Boston Celtics and Miami Heat Are Officially Rivals|work=[[Bleacher Report]]|date=July 14, 2012|accessdate=March 23, 2023}}</ref>

Near the end of 2010, ''[[The New York Times]]'' wrote on a Celtics win over the [[New York Knicks]]: "With their win over the Knicks on Wednesday, the Celtics conquered the NBA, though Boston fans now demonize the Miami Heat as surrogate [[New York Yankees|Yankees]]," referencing the [[Red Sox–Yankees rivalry]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Tanier|first=Mark|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2010/12/19/sports/19rivalry.html|url-access=subscription|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140811011406/https://www.nytimes.com/2010/12/19/sports/19rivalry.html|title=On the East Coast, a Three-City Rivalry Transformed|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=December 19, 2010|accessdate=March 23, 2023|archive-date=August 11, 2014}}</ref>

[[File:Dwyane Wade and LeBron James.jpg|thumb|left|250px|[[Dwyane Wade]] and [[LeBron James]] helped propel the Heat over the Celtics in the 2011 and 2012 postseasons]]
Now with James and Bosh on the roster, the two teams met in the [[2011 NBA playoffs#(2) Miami Heat vs. (3) Boston Celtics|2011 Eastern Conference Semifinals]]. As the #2-seed, the Heat had home court advantage over the #3-seed Celtics. James called the series "personal" for him, citing his losses to the Celtics while a member of the Cavaliers.<ref>{{cite web|last=Reynolds|first=Tim|url=https://www.staugustine.com/story/sports/2011/05/01/lebron-gets-another-shot-celtics/16206202007/|title=LeBron gets another shot at Celtics|work=[[The St. Augustine Record]]|publisher=[[Gannett]]|date=May 1, 2011|accessdate=March 23, 2023}}</ref> In Game 5 of the series, Wade and James scored 34 and 33, respectively.<ref name=Beck>{{cite web|last=Beck|first=Howard|author-link=Howard Beck|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2011/05/12/sports/basketball/james-leads-late-run-as-heat-closes-out-celtics.html|url-access=subscription|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110515030207/https://www.nytimes.com/2011/05/12/sports/basketball/james-leads-late-run-as-heat-closes-out-celtics.html|title=Heat Overcomes the Celtics|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=May 12, 2011|accessdate=March 23, 2023|archive-date=May 15, 2011}}</ref> James went on a 10–0 scoring run to close out game, securing a 4–1 series win for the Heat. The Celtics and Heat once again faced off in the postseason in 2012, this time in the [[2012 NBA playoffs#(2) Miami Heat vs. (4) Boston Celtics|Eastern Conference finals]] (ECF).<ref>{{cite web|last=Beck|first=Howard|author-link=Howard Beck|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2012/05/29/sports/basketball/nba-playoffs-heat-beat-celtics-james-scores-32.html|url-access=subscription|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120531224435/https://www.nytimes.com/2012/05/29/sports/basketball/nba-playoffs-heat-beat-celtics-james-scores-32.html|title=Heat's James and Wade Continue Domination|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=May 29, 2012|accessdate=March 23, 2023|archive-date=May 31, 2012}}</ref> The Heat were the #2-seed while the Celtics were the #4-seed, giving the Heat home court advantage. James fouled out of Game 4, while Wade missed a potential game-winning basket at the buzzer.<ref>{{cite web|last=Golliver|first=Ben|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/video-heat-f-lebron-james-fouls-out-in-game-4-overtime-loss-to-celtics/|title= Video: Heat F LeBron James fouls out in Game 4 overtime loss to Celtics |work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=June 3, 2012|accessdate=March 23, 2023}}</ref> Later, down 3–2 in the series, the Heat went on the road to face the Celtics in game six of the series. Helping the Heat tie the series, James had 45 points, 15 rebounds, and five assists.<ref>{{cite web|last=Green|first=Austin|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1213505-heat-vs-celtics-game-6-highlights-twitter-reaction-and-analysis|title=Heat vs. Celtics: Game 6 Highlights, Twitter Reaction and Analysis|work=[[Bleacher Report]]|date=June 7, 2012|accessdate=March 23, 2023}}</ref> Praised by basketball media at the time,<ref name=Gregory/><ref>{{cite web|last=Emerick|first=Peter|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1213544-ranking-lebrons-epic-game-6-with-all-time-best-individual-playoff-performances|title=Ranking LeBron's Epic Game 6 with All-Time Individual Playoff Performances|work=[[Bleacher Report]]|date=June 8, 2012|accessdate=March 23, 2023}}</ref> sportswriters have also retrospectively noted James' game six performance as one of his best and most important.<ref>{{cite web|last=Winfield|first=Kristian|url=https://www.sbnation.com/2017/6/7/15758680/lebron-james-five-5-year-anniversary-vs-celtics-cavs-vs-warriors-2017-nba-finals|title=LeBron James crafted his greatest playoff moment 5 years ago today. He'll need to do it again|work=[[SB Nation]]|date=June 7, 2017|accessdate=March 23, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Huff|first=Cole|url=https://ftw.usatoday.com/2022/05/flashback-lebron-james-45-points-boston-celtics-game-6-2012|title=Flashback Friday: LeBron scores 45 vs. Celtics in legendary Game 6 performance in 2012|work=[[USA Today]]|date=May 27, 2022|accessdate=March 23, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Squadron|first=Alex|url=https://www.slamonline.com/nba/throwback-lebron-dropped-45-points-2012-ecf-game-6-win-celtics/|title=THROWBACK: LeBron Dropped 45 Points In 2012 ECF Game 6 Win Over Celtics 👑|work=[[Slam (magazine)|Slam]]|date=May 12, 2018|accessdate=March 23, 2023}}</ref> The Heat won the series 4–3 after winning Game 7 by a score of 101–88.<ref name=Gregory/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/320609014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230324034139/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/320609014|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 24, 2023|title=LeBron James, Heat pull away from Celtics, advance to NBA Finals|agency=[[Associated Press]]|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=June 10, 2012|accessdate=March 23, 2023}}</ref> James later stated that he feared a loss to the Celtics in 2012 would have caused the Heat's Big Three to break up before winning a championship.<ref name=KaskeyBlomain>{{cite web|last=Kaskey-Blomain|first=Michael|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/lebron-james-feared-that-loss-to-celtics-in-2012-would-cause-heats-big-3-to-break-up-tarnish-his-legacy/|title= LeBron James feared that loss to Celtics in 2012 would cause Heat's 'Big 3' to break up, tarnish his legacy |work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=March 20, 2020|accessdate=March 23, 2023}}</ref>

With these three straight postseason meetings, the Heat's rivalry with the Celtics became their most notable since their [[Heat–Knicks rivalry|rivalry with the Knicks]], according to ''[[Bleacher Report]]''.<ref name=Weiss>{{cite web|last=Weiss|first=David|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1419795-ranking-the-5-biggest-heat-rivals-by-level-of-hatred|title=Ranking the 5 Biggest Miami Heat Rivals by Level of Hatred|work=[[Bleacher Report]]|date=November 23, 2012|accessdate=March 23, 2023}}</ref> Boston's [[Rajon Rondo]] also played a pivotal role in the rivalry during this period. Writing for ''[[Business Insider]]'', Tony Manfred stated much of the rivalry was based on off-court narratives, but called Rondo "the only reason these two team have an actual on-court rivalry."<ref name=Manfred>{{cite web|last=Manfred|first=Tony|url=https://www.businessinsider.com/rajon-rondo-celtics-heat-2012-10|title=Rajon Rondo Is The One Player In The East Who Can Stop The Heat|work=[[Business Insider]]|date=October 30, 2012|accessdate=March 23, 2023}}</ref> Writing for ''Bleacher Report'', Jason Reindollar called the rivalry between the two teams "official" following their 2012 ECF matchup.<ref name=Reindollar/>

{{multiple image
| align = right
| direction = horizontal

During the offseason, Allen signed with the Heat.<ref name=Villa>{{cite web|last=Villa|first=Walter|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2012/11/01/sports/basketball/miami-heat-start-nba-season-where-they-left-off.html|url-access=subscription|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121101054157/https://www.nytimes.com/2012/11/01/sports/basketball/miami-heat-start-nba-season-where-they-left-off.html|title=Heat Celebrate Their Title, and Start Building on It|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=November 1, 2012|accessdate=March 23, 2023|archive-date=November 1, 2012}}</ref> A rift between Allen and Rondo was cited as a factor for Allen's departure from Boston.<ref name=Manfred/> Garnett, Rondo, and Pierce were reported to hold a grudge with Allen for multiple years after.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/boston/boston-celtics/why-didnt-rajon-rondo-comment-on-ray-allen-miami-heat-during-boston-celtics-reunion-with-kevin-garnett-paul-pierce-kendrick-perkins-glen-davis?b|title=Rajon Rondo was the only one to stay quiet during Ray Allen discussion|publisher=[[NBC Sports]]|date=May 9, 2017|accessdate=March 23, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=|first=|url=https://celticswire.usatoday.com/2018/09/08/celtics-ray-allen-rajon-rondo-doc-rivers-drama/|title=
Ray Allen opens up about what happened in final year with Celtics|work=[[USA Today]]|date=September 8, 2018|accessdate=March 23, 2023}}</ref> [[Doc Rivers]], who coached the Celtics from 2004 to 2013, has discussed the rift and taken blame for it.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/boston/celtics/why-doc-rivers-blames-himself-ray-allens-rift-2008-celtics|title=Why Doc Rivers blames himself for Ray Allen's rift with 2008 Celtics|publisher=[[NBC Sports]]|date=April 3, 2020|accessdate=March 23, 2023}}</ref> The two teams opened up their [[2012–13 NBA season]] playing against each other in Miami.<ref>{{cite web|last=Baradwaj|first=Nikhil|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1286125-is-the-boston-celtics-vs-miami-heat-the-best-rivalry-in-the-nba|title=Is Boston Celtics vs. Miami Heat the Best Rivalry in the NBA?|work=[[Bleacher Report]]|date=August 7, 2012|accessdate=March 23, 2023}}</ref> The game continued the rivalry's intense and physical nature, with Rondo being noted to grab Wade around the neck in the game.<ref name=Villa/> During the season, the Heat achieved a 27-game win streak, which included a game against the Celtics. The game featured James finishing a [[fast break]] by dunking on [[Jason Terry]], a "personal rival" of James' according to [[Brian Windhorst]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Windhorst|first=Brian|author-link=Brian Windhorst|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/truehoop/miamiheat/story/_/id/9075039/lebron-james-miami-heat-says-posterizing-boston-celtics-jason-terry-was-pleasure|title=LeBron James to Terry: In your face!|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=March 20, 2013|accessdate=March 23, 2023}}</ref>

The two front offices would get involved in the rivalry in the middle of the 2012–13 season. During a radio interview, Celtics general manager [[Danny Ainge]] criticized James for his complaints about officiating, causing Heat general manager [[Pat Riley]] to issue a statement, saying: "Danny Ainge needs to shut the fuck up and manage his own team. He was the biggest whiner going when he was playing, and I know that because I coached against him."<ref name="Windhorst">{{cite web|last=Windhorst|first=Brian|author-link=Brian Windhorst|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/page/presents-19771331/brian-windhorst-danny-ainge-pat-riley-wooing-hayward-nba|title=The Gordon Hayward chase pits worthy adversaries Ainge, Riley|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=June 30, 2017|accessdate=May 17, 2023}}</ref> In response, Ainge would issue a statement of his own: "I stand by what I said. That's all. I don't care about Pat Riley. He can say whatever he wants. I don't want to mess up his Armani suits and all that hair goop. It would be way too expensive for me."<ref>{{cite web |last=Geagan |first=Matthew |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/boston/news/danny-ainge-pat-riley-feud-celtics-heat-easternc-conference-finals-nba-playoffs/ |title=Will We Get Another Chapter Of The Danny Ainge-Pat Riley Feud During Celtics–Heat Eastern Conference Finals?|publisher=[[CBS News Boston]]|date=September 14, 2020 |accessdate=May 18, 2023}}</ref> The two were noted to have a personal rivalry stemming for 30 years, dating back to when Ainge played for the Celtics and Riley was the head coach of the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], which itself was a [[Celtics–Lakers rivalry|very storied team rivalry]].<ref name="Windhorst" /> Ainge would eventually tell ''[[The Boston Globe]]'' "we're both right. LeBron should stop complaining and I should manage my own team." Both head coaches expressed amusement with the exchange between their general managers, with Rivers calling it "cool" and jokingly suggesting that Riley and Ainge "should duke it out", and Heat coach [[Erik Spoelstra]] stating "I love direct GM to GM communication. That's awesome."<ref name="providence">{{cite web |last=Winderman |first=Ira |url=https://www.providencejournal.com/story/sports/nba/2013/03/30/20130329-riley-ainge-feud-goes-to-another-level-ece/35332122007/ |title=Riley, Ainge feud goes to another level |publisher=[[The Providence Journal]]|date=March 29, 2013|accessdate=May 17, 2023}}</ref>

The Heat did not meet the Celtics in the [[2013 NBA playoffs|2013 postseason]], but Allen helped the Heat win their second consecutive championship with a clutch game-tying shot in game six of the [[2013 NBA Finals|Finals]].<ref name=Jenkins>{{cite magazine|last=Jenkins|first=Lee|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2013/12/18/ray-allen-miami-heat-29-seconds-nba-finals-game-6|title=Anatomy Of A Miracle: Ray Allen's shot in Game 6|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=December 18, 2013|accessdate=March 23, 2023}}</ref>

The Celtics and Heat once again met in the [[2020 NBA playoffs#(3) Boston Celtics vs. (5) Miami Heat|Eastern Conference Finals]] in 2020.<ref name=Reynolds2020>{{cite web|last=Reynolds|first=Tim|url=https://www.boston.com/sports/boston-celtics/2020/09/12/celtics-jaylen-brown-jayson-tatum-marcus-smart-heat-eastern-conference-finals/|title=Celtics' young core heads back to East finals, once again|website=[[Boston.com]]|date=September 12, 2020|accessdate=March 24, 2023}}</ref> The Heat's [[Udonis Haslem]] was the only remaining player from the two teams' prior playoff meeting.<ref>{{cite web|last=Quinn|first=Sam|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/celtics-vs-raptors-score-boston-holds-on-to-pull-off-win-in-game-7-over-toronto/live/|title= Celtics vs. Raptors score: Boston holds on to pull off win in Game 7 over Toronto |work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=September 12, 2020|accessdate=March 23, 2023}}</ref> The #3-seed Celtics were led by a core of [[Jayson Tatum]], [[Jaylen Brown]], and [[Marcus Smart]].<ref name=Reynolds2020/> The #5-seed Heat were led by [[Jimmy Butler]] and [[Bam Adebayo]].<ref name=Deb>{{cite web|last=Deb|first=Sopan|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/09/27/sports/basketball/nba-heat-celtics-finals.html|url-access=subscription|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200928024004/https://www.nytimes.com/2020/09/27/sports/basketball/nba-heat-celtics-finals.html|title=Miami Heat Advance to the N.B.A. Finals|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=September 27, 2020|accessdate=March 24, 2023|archive-date=September 28, 2020}}</ref> The series took place at a neutral "[[2020 NBA Bubble|bubble]]" site in Orlando due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-basketball-nba-bos-hayward/celtics-hayward-wont-leave-bubble-for-babys-birth-idUSKCN26B0M0|title=Celtics' Hayward won't leave bubble for baby's birth|publisher=[[Reuters]]|date=September 20, 2020|accessdate=March 24, 2023}}</ref><ref name=Schuhmann2022>{{cite web|last=Schuhmann|first=John|url=https://www.nba.com/news/series-preview-heat-celtics-clash-in-rematch-of-2020-eastern-conference-finals|title=Series preview: Heat, Celtics square off with Finals berth on the line|website=[[National Basketball Association|NBA.com]]|publisher=[[National Basketball Association]]|date=May 15, 2022|accessdate=March 24, 2023}}</ref> During Game 4, rookie Heat guard [[Tyler Herro]] scored 37 points, becoming the fourth player aged 20 or younger to score 30 points in the NBA playoffs.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4235458/2020/09/24/tyler-herros-37-lead-heat-over-celtics-in-eastern-conference-finals-game-4/|title=Tyler Herro's 37 lead Heat over Celtics in Eastern Conference finals Game 4|work=[[The Athletic]]|date=September 23, 2020|access-date=March 24, 2023}}</ref> The Heat won the series in six games.<ref name=Deb/>

Two years later, the Celtics and Heat faced off against each other in another ECF matchup, with the Heat as the #1-seed and the Celtics as the #2-seed.<ref name=Schuhmann2022/> Sportswriters noted the series as having drastic swings, calling it an "ugly" and "physical, back-and-forth" affair.<ref name=Buckner>{{cite news|last=Buckner|first=Candace|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2022/05/24/celtics-heat-blowouts-eastern-conference-finals/|url-access=subscription|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220524123429/https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2022/05/24/celtics-heat-blowouts-eastern-conference-finals/|title=The Celtics–Heat series is a loopy, inexplicable mystery|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|date=May 24, 2022|accessdate=March 24, 2023|archive-date=May 24, 2022}}</ref><ref name=Mannix/><ref name=OConnor>{{cite web|last=O'Connor|first=Kevin|url=https://www.theringer.com/2022/5/30/23147114/boston-celtics-miami-heat-jayson-tatum-takeaways|title=
Takeaways From a Weird and Wild Game 7 of the Eastern Conference Finals|publisher=[[The Ringer (website)|The Ringer]]|date=May 30, 2022|accessdate=March 24, 2023}}</ref> Writing for ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'', Chris Mannix commented that game five was a particularly bad viewing experience, citing the two teams' poor offensive performances.<ref name=Mannix>{{cite magazine|last=Mannix|first=Chris|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2022/05/26/celtics-heat-game-5-ugly-win-boston-finals|title=Celtics Inch Closer to Finals With Ugly Game 5 Win|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=May 26, 2022|accessdate=March 24, 2023}}</ref> Down 3–2 in the series, Butler scored 47 points, while also grabbing nine rebounds and recording eight assists to help Miami force a Game 7.<ref name=Winderman>{{cite web|last=Winderman|first=Ira|url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-heat/fl-sp-miami-heat-boston-celtics-game-6-20220528-mobyfmodgff2hlt7jquwdzkixi-story.html|title=Jimmy Butler conjures his LeBron James with 47 as Heat force Game 7 with 111–103 win in Boston|work=[[Sun-Sentinel|Sun Sentinel]]|date=May 28, 2022|accessdate=March 24, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Golen|first=Jimmy|url=https://apnews.com/article/miami-heat-boston-celtics-nba-mlb-sports-e63d7424bb2a61e590b6e1a544c32f88|title=Butler scores 47 points, Heat beat Celtics to force Game 7|work=[[Associated Press]]|date=May 28, 2022|accessdate=March 24, 2023}}</ref> Butler's performance drew comparisons to James' 45-point performance from a decade prior.<ref name=Winderman/><ref>{{cite web|last=Vardon|first=Joe|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4176639/2022/05/28/jimmy-butlers-47-points-help-heat-force-game-7-vs-celtics-in-eastern-conference-finals/|url-access=subscription|title=Jimmy Butler's 47 points help Heat force Game 7 vs. Celtics in Eastern Conference finals|work=[[The Athletic]]|date=May 27, 2022|access-date=March 24, 2023}}</ref> Down by two with under a minute left in the game, Butler attempted a three-pointer to put the Heat ahead but missed.<ref name=GanguliCacciola>{{cite web|last1=Ganguli|first1=Tania|last2=Cacciola|first2=Scott|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/05/29/sports/basketball/boston-celtics-miami-heat-game-7-nba-finals.html|url-access=subscription|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220603000024/https://www.nytimes.com/2022/05/29/sports/basketball/boston-celtics-miami-heat-game-7-nba-finals.html|title=Boston Celtics Beat Miami Heat in Game 7 for Trip to N.B.A. Finals|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=June 2, 2022|orig-date=May 29, 2022|accessdate=March 24, 2023|archive-date=June 3, 2022}}</ref> The Celtics defeated the Heat 100–96 on the road in Game 7, winning the series and clinching a berth to the [[2022 NBA Finals]].<ref name=GanguliCacciola/> It also was Boston's first postseason win against Miami since 2010. [[Jayson Tatum]] scored 26 points in the game for the Celtics and was awarded the inaugural Eastern Conference Finals MVP award, dubbed the [[Larry Bird Trophy]].<ref name=GanguliCacciola/>

The NBA introduced a "Rivals Week" in the 2022–23 season; the Heat and Celtics faced off against each other during the week.<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Siegel|first=Brett|url=https://www.si.com/fannation/nba/fastbreak/news/2022-23-nba-rivalry-week-celtics-lakers-heat-nets-knicks-76ers-suns-mavericks-grizzlies-warriors|title=2022–23 NBA Schedule: Examining League's New "Rivals Week" Matchups|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=August 19, 2022|accessdate=March 25, 2023}}</ref> The two teams once again met in the [[2023 NBA playoffs|2023 Eastern Conference Finals]], with the Celtics entering the series as the #2-seed and the Heat as the #8-seed.<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Richardson|first=Shandel|url=https://www.si.com/nba/heat/miami-news/miami-heat-to-face-boston-celtics-in-eastern-conference-finals-for-second-straight-season|title=Miami Heat To Face Boston Celtics In Eastern Conference Finals For Second Straight Season|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=May 14, 2023|accessdate=May 15, 2023}}</ref> Prior to the series, ESPN Analytics gave the Heat a 3% chance of making the Finals.<ref>{{cite web|last=Clark|first=Geoff|url=https://www.outkick.com/espn-analytics-is-trending-because-it-is-dumb/|title=ESPN Analytics is Trending Because it is Dumb|work=[[OutKick]]|date=May 20, 2022|accessdate=June 11, 2023}}</ref> Despite this, Miami took a 3–0 series lead. The Celtics would respond by winning the next three games, punctuated with a go-ahead shot with 0.2 seconds left on the clock by [[Derrick White]] during Game 6 in Miami. In doing so, the Celtics became the fourth team in NBA history to force a Game 7 after going down 0–3, and the only one to force a Game 7 at home.<ref>{{cite web|last=Goss|first=Nick|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/boston/celtics/nba-highlights-derrick-white-extends-celtics-season-game-6-buzzer-beater |title=Derrick White extends Celtics' season with epic Game 6 buzzer-beater |publisher=[[NBC Sports]]|date=May 27, 2023|accessdate=May 30, 2023}}</ref> Tatum injured his ankle on the first possession of Game 7, though remained in the game.<ref>{{cite web|last=Friedell|first=Nick|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/37757464/heat-stomp-celtics-game-7-carry-dream-run-nba-finals|title=Heat stomp Celtics in G7, become second No. 8 seed to make Finals|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=May 27, 2023|accessdate=May 30, 2023}}</ref> Miami won the deciding game in Boston, resulting in the Heat becoming the second #8-seed in NBA history to reach the Finals and avoiding the distinction of becoming the first team to squander a 3–0 playoff series lead. Butler won the Larry Bird Trophy as the Eastern Conference finals MVP, succeeding Tatum.

In the [[2023–24 NBA season]], the Celtics were dominant, winning a league-leading 64 games in the regular season and clinching the #1-seed in the East.<ref>{{cite web|last=Reiter|first=Bill|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/celtics-playoff-path-set-up-perfectly-in-must-win-postseason-will-it-lead-to-redemption-or-disappointment/|title= Celtics' playoff path set up perfectly in must-win postseason -- will it lead to redemption or disappointment? |publisher=[[CBS Sports]]|date=April 24, 2024|accessdate=June 25, 2024}}</ref> Conversely, the Heat narrowly made the playoffs, clinching the #8-seed through the [[NBA play-in tournament|play-in tournament]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Chiang|first=Anthony|url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/nba/miami-heat/article287810700.html|title=Takeaways from Butler-less Heat's playoff-clinching win over Bulls and a look at what's ahead|work=[[The Miami Herald]]|date=April 20, 2024|accessdate=June 25, 2024}}</ref> The two teams met in the first round of the playoffs, though the Heat were without Butler for the series due to a knee injury he sustained in the play-in.<ref>{{cite web|last=Maloney|first=Jack|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/jimmy-butler-injury-update-heat-star-out-for-entire-first-round-playoff-series-vs-celtics-per-report/|title= Jimmy Butler injury update: Heat star out for entire first-round playoff series vs. Celtics, per report |publisher=[[CBS Sports]]|date=April 22, 2024|accessdate=June 25, 2024}}</ref> The series was tied after two games, with the Heat setting a franchise playoff record for three-pointers made in Game 2, though the Celtics were able to dispatch the Heat in five games en route to a [[2024 NBA Finals]] victory.<ref>{{cite web|last=Golen|first=Jimmy|url=https://www.nba.com/news/heat-franchise-playoff-record-3-pointers|title=Heat set franchise playoff record with 23 3-pointers in Game 2 win|work=[[The Associated Press]]|via=[[NBA.com]]|date=April 24, 2024|accessdate=June 25, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Buckley|first=Steve|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5572535/2024/06/18/garden-party-celtics-nba-champions-book/|title=Garden Party: Celtics win record 18th NBA championship to cap a dominant season|work=[[The Athletic]]|via=''[[The New York Times]]''|date=June 18, 2024|accessdate=June 25, 2024}}</ref>
